newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA END EFFORTS TO PERSUADE DUNDEE TO STAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA END EFFORTS TO PERSUADE DUNDEE TO STAY.

text.p: South Africa have decided to end efforts to persuade striker Sean Dundee to join their World Cup squad as he moves closer to a career in international soccer with Germany.

South African coach Clive Barker said on Wednesday he had concluded attempts to convince the 23-year-old striker to change his mind and opt to play for the country of his birth during the qualifying campaign for the 1998 World Cup finals in France.

Dundee, who plays for German club Karlsruhe and is the leading goalscorer in the Bundesliga, is hoping to become a naturalised German citizen soon in order to play for Germany in their World Cup qualifying tie against Northern Ireland next month.

The Durban-born forward has spurned numerous call-ups from South Africa, who in turn have accused the German coach Berti Vogts of poaching the player and putting pressure on Dundee to play for Germany instead of South Africa.

Dundee's intentions have caused an uproar in South Africa with the matter even being discussed in Parliament, while German legislators have also questions the haste with which his naturalisation application is being dealt with.
Barker continued his attack on Vogts for his alleged role in swaying Dundee's decision and also questioned Germany's need for the player in view of their massive playing resources.
"They have a huge infra-structure and have one of the top leagues in the world. We are a nation emerging from a 30-year isolation period. Do they really need him?" Barker asked.

The South African coach has been under pressure in recent weeks to drop his attempts to lure Dundee home for the country's World Cup campaign, which starts in earnest on November 9 against Zaire in Johannesburg.
A vast majority of radio talkshow callers and letters to newspaper editors have expressed anger at Dundee's decision and Barker's continuing efforts to call him into the South African squad.
Dundee told South African newspapers last week that criticism levelled at him had been unfair.
"I have signed a seven-year contract with my club and my future is in Germany. Don't spurn me, support me," he said.

Barker rejected comparing Dundee's decision to those of other South African sportspeople, such as cricketers Kepler Wessels, Allan Lamb, track athletes Zola Budd, Sydney Maree and Mark Plaatjes, the former world marathon champion.
"Those people had no choice if they wanted international competition during the time South African sport was isolated. Dundee had a choice," he said.
"Nevertheless, I wish Dundee every bit of success with his new country."
